A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and matchable. v1 ends after the references despite mentioning supplementary material; v2 includes Appendices A–H. The comparison covers the material actually supplied.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-estimation results on nuScenes, ZJU-4DRadarCam and View-of-Delft, with backbone comparisons, polynomial-degree experiments and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and additionally reports computational efficiency, cross-dataset transfer, radar sparsity, regression comparisons and monotonicity analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces dot-product prototype aggregation with temperature-controlled, distance-based soft clustering. It also introduces sinusoidal 3D radar embeddings and learned 2D positional embeddings in fusion, supported by a new embedding ablation. These change important representation components, while polynomial prediction and the three-term loss remain.

E1.justification: The three datasets and radar-camera depth-estimation task remain. Appendix G adds zero-shot nuScenes-to-ZJU/VoD transfer and reduced-radar-input scenarios, extending coverage to domain transfer and degraded sensing conditions within the existing driving domain.

E2.justification: v2 adds TacoDepth to nuScenes/ZJU accuracy comparisons, numerous methods including NLSPN, BPNet and CaFNet in Table 7, and isotonic/spline regression plus LoRA and ViT-Adapter in Table 13. Lin's nuScenes results move to Table 7, while its ZJU/VoD accuracy comparisons disappear.

E3.justification: The main MAE/RMSE evaluations at 50, 70 and 80 meters remain. New protocols measure training time, inference latency and GFLOPs; evaluate source-trained models on target datasets; retain specified radar fractions; introduce learned-point controls; and measure ordinal agreement using Kendall's tau. These extend evaluation design substantially.

E4.justification: v1's backbone, polynomial-degree and component studies largely reappear in Appendix A. v2 adds positional-embedding and learned-point ablations, zero-shot transfer, radar-density robustness, quantitative depth-ordering analysis and VoD qualitative case studies. These test additional questions about spatial information, radar dependence and generalization.

E5.justification: v1 reports no corresponding statistical assessment. Appendix G introduces 30 bootstrap samples for Kendall's tau and a two-sample t-test comparing POLAR with raw MDE, reporting p = 0.012. This is a localized addition; bootstrap samples do not establish repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the proposed method's nuScenes results: at 80 meters, MAE/RMSE change from 1454.1/3488.9 to 1407.8/3193.5, while its main ZJU/VoD entries remain unchanged. v2 adds extensive efficiency, comparator, transfer and robustness results. Its Table 6 VoD full-model entry conflicts with Table 1, so that entry cannot support a reliable performance interpretation.

T1.justification: Appendix H adds a constructive proposition proving that some sets of three or more depth pairs cannot share an affine fit, followed by a polynomial-approximation corollary. Appendix B derives incremental polynomial computation costs. These provide limited formal extensions to v1's existing mathematical motivation.

C1.justification: v2 elevates efficiency into a headline contribution, claiming state-of-the-art latency and computational cost and over 40 fps, beyond v1's general efficiency assertions. The abstract's reported MAE/RMSE advantages change from 30.3%/37.2% to 24.9%/33.2% alongside the expanded comparisons. The central polynomial-fitting contribution remains.

C2.justification: Appendix G interprets new controls as evidence of actual radar dependence, attributes regression-baseline shortcomings to radar noise, and discusses possible depth inversions using the new monotonicity analysis. Section 4.2 connects measured efficiency to deployment practicality. The stated limitations concerning degree selection and polynomial oscillation remain.

D1.justification: Appendices C and F newly supply dataset sizes, split descriptions, sensors, image crops, 60 training epochs, a cosine learning-rate schedule starting at 5e-5, and loss weights of 1.0/0.4/0.25. Table 2 identifies an NVIDIA A6000 for training-time measurements. These substantially improve documentation without establishing changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v2 updates positioning with TacoDepth, LoRA, ViT-Adapter, BPNet and additional benchmark references, while pruning older discussion and citations such as CSPN/CSPN++ and R4Dyn. Its central distinction between polynomial scene fitting and direct completion or fusion remains.

P1.justification: PolyRad becomes POLAR throughout. The abstract, contribution statement and regularization explanations are revised; Section 3.2 gains component-specific organization; and comparative studies move from main Section 4.2 to Appendix A. Computational efficiency replaces them in the main experimental narrative, with additional material organized into eight appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, with extensive reflow and relocation. The original qualitative and polynomial illustrations remain with exchanged figure numbering. v2 adds efficiency and diagnostic tables, shared colorbars, VoD examples, radar-versus-lidar visualizations and a counterexample plot.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of the method through stronger comparators, explicit radar-dependence and robustness controls, measured computational efficiency, and previously missing training details. These address important evidential and reproducibility weaknesses in v1. The gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including Table 6's inconsistent VoD entry and Appendix A percentage improvements that are not supported by Table 4.
